utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC
utterances.text: "Pursuant to Article 7 of the decision on the organisation and work of the Crisis Staff of Prijedor Municipality at the session held on 5th of June, 1992, the Crisis Staff of Prijedor Municipality issues the following order: It is hereby forbidden every unauthorised shooting from fire weapons in the territory of Prijedor Municipality. "Second, the consistent implementation of this order will be under the authority of the police and the public security organs of Prijedor, which will take the legally prescribed actions against the -- all those who violate this order. "This order shall come into effect immediately."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Do you agree that this is an order directed, amongst others, to the military police? An order by the Crisis Staff, and as it is reflected in the Official Gazette, by Dr. Milomir Stakic, president of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC
utterances.text: Yes, I've read it. This is obvious. But the question I raise here is whether this decision was valid before the military bodies, before the military prosecution at that time in our parts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May we then proceed to page number 42 in the English version. It's item 30, 3-0. Due to the short time, I want to direct you immediately under the word "Order," paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC
utterances.text: "Hereby the command of the Prijedor garrison and the public security station are hereby duty-bound to establish the needs to engage the materiel equipment and deliver to the municipal secretariat for national defence in order to legalise the fact that technical equipment and materiel have been taken by the military and the police in keeping with their actual needs."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Would it be correct to draw the inference from this order directed to the Prijedor garrison command that this is, in fact, maybe the attempt only, but it reflects an order directed to box number 5 in the sketch you have drawn?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC
utterances.text: The brigades? I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The Prijedor garrison command. Just some minutes ago, you told us that you would allocate the Prijedor garrison command in box 5. So therefore, would this document reflect an order vis-a-vis this fifth box in your sketch on Exhibit Number D50B?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC
utterances.text: Possibly, as an attempt to realise the interests that politics or certain circles from the Crisis Staff had. But it was an attempt, an endeavour on their part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May we then turn to item number 48. This is on the English version on page number 51. Would you please read aloud this order.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC
utterances.text: "Pursuant to Articles 3 and 7 of the decision on the organisation and work of the Crisis Staff of Prijedor Municipality, the Crisis Staff of Prijedor Municipality, at a session held on the 17th of June 1992 and in connection with information on the security situation on the territory of Prijedor Municipality, makes the -- issues the following order: "It orders the public security station of Prijedor and the regional command of Prijedor, within a space of two days, to form a uniform intervention platoon -- a united intervention platoon with 20 members, the basic task of which will be to prevent looting and other criminal undertakings on the territory of the municipality, and the movement of all unregistered vehicles and vehicles carrying members of the army and police force without travel permits, without regularly issued travel permits. "The composition of the platoon from the previous item will be made up of the regional command and the public security station. These are duty-bound within the space of -- a space of seven days to report back to the Crisis Staff in the municipality in writing on the activities and results of the work of the intervention platoon. "This order comes into effect on the day it was issued."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: What would be your comment on this order?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC
utterances.text: The same as before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And if you could, please, repeat. Is this an order directed to the Prijedor regional command?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC
utterances.text: Yes, and that's what it says here, to the Regional Command of Prijedor, whereas I said that as far as -- I said how far I was familiar with the regional command as a body. That's what I was talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Related to this document, I was able to understand the content of the document, but if you move forward to item number 55, here I really want -- need your assistance in understanding this document. If you could read it aloud first, please.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC
utterances.text: "At the session held on the 29th of May, 1992, at 16.30 hours, the Crisis Staff of Prijedor makes the following provision: "1. It relieves of duty the commander of the Serbian territorial defence, Major Slobodan Kuruzovic. This comes into effect on the 29th of May, 1992. And he shall be placed under the command of the regional command. "This decision comes into effect immediately. And the Crisis Staff of Prijedor Municipality and the command of the region shall see that it is implemented."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: What does it mean here "placed under the command of the command of the region"?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence existed in peacetime, as far as I understand, and this was a reserve component. In certain municipalities, the Territorial Defence had its departments, and their task in peacetime was to call the reservists up for training, at intervals. And with the war, or rather in 1992 - I don't know the exact date - the units of the Territorial Defence as a Territorial Defence ceased to exist. Now, whether the Crisis Staff could have replaced and subordinated this to the region, I don't know. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And then finally, item number 101. English, page number 70.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC
utterances.text: "Pursuant to Articles 3 and 7 of the decision pertaining to the organisation and work of the Crisis Staff of Prijedor Municipality, the Crisis Staff of Prijedor Municipality at its session held on the 12th of June, 1992, adopts the following conclusion: "1. That it be suggested to the autonomous province of Krajina to set up a Crisis Staff which would be made up of all the presidents of the Municipal Assemblies and the hitherto staff be transformed into a Crisis Staff of Banja Luka municipality. "2. The autonomous province of Krajina is called upon to set up the urgent formation of a government for the autonomous province of Krajina and the autonomous province of Krajina is requested to provide explanations as to the conclusions made by the Crisis Staff, which refers to the pensioning off of workers who have served 30 and 35 -- who have done 30 and 35 years of service. This conclusion comes into effect on the day it was passed." This is slightly illegible. Perhaps I read something incorrectly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Your comments on this document.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC
utterances.text: This document is a sort of political platform, if I can call it that. It is derived from the political platform and interests of the political parties. As far as I know, I don't remember actually that anything of this kind was set up in Banja Luka, or that we were under the influence of the Crisis Staff, that is to say the army in Banja Luka, and especially my own medical corps. I don't recall being under their influence at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Unfortunately, I missed one item, and this was 97. If you could have a look on this as well, and read it aloud. English, page number 69.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC
utterances.text: "At its session held on the 29th of May, 1992, the Crisis Staff of Prijedor Municipality adopts the following conclusion: With the formation of the army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the need ceases to exist for the existence of the Serbian TO, which shall become part of the composition and come under the command of the region. This conclusion comes into effect immediately. And the Crisis Staff of Prijedor Municipality, along with the regional command, will see that it is put into practice."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: From your point of view, what does this conclusion reflect, being yourself in your capacity as a physician, member of the army, would know about the results on the formation on the army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina? Can you tell us something about this development apparently concluded by the formation of this army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I did not understand your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: My question was, leaving aside the text of this document, had the formation of the army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina any impact on your individual work and the entire structure and the hierarchy of the army?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC
utterances.text: If you mean professionally and professional advancement, and the training of medical corps staff in Republika Srpska, during the war, in wartime, it wasn't at a very high level, I have to admit. And we didn't have the material resources or the time, because of our daily duties and obligations, to devote more work to training. We had to work with the sick and wounded. So that there was not much progress made in the sense of training and education for our staff members.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The last question from my side for today, coming now back to your initial testimony, where on your own sketch would you allocate the army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC
utterances.text: Your Honour, did you mean this particular diagram?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC
utterances.text: The army of Republika Srpska ranged from the main staff right down to the troops, the soldiers. So to all intents and purposes, all these commands of the individual units comprised the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And why was it so that apparently following this conclusion, it was -- it seemed to be appropriate that the Serbian TO shall be incorporated into the structure of the region and placed under its command? Where would you put the Serbian Territorial Defence in the hierarchy of your own sketch?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR PUSAC
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't answer that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. I think in all likelihood, the Defence will have a number of questions, and also the Judges will have a number of questions. With a view to the watch, it's absolutely necessary to have a break, and I think we have to continue a longer period of time tomorrow. May I, therefore, ask you, please be so kind and not contact any of the parties - no representative of the Prosecution, no representative of the Defence - until we resume; and the same is true, please don't contact any other witnesses you might by chance meet here, there, and everywhere in The Hague. It often happens, unfortunately. But please be so kind, in order to establish a fair trial, that you don't speak with these persons. I thank you for today's long testimony and hope to meet you tomorrow once again in a fresh condition. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The trial stays adjourned until tomorrow, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
